spec_features.spec_quote: an instrument designed to *induce* distress-like states is, if those states matter at all, also a thing that could cause them
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. The only code echo is the __init__.py docstring 'Ethical note' (welfare_eval/__init__.py:8-11), a docstring, not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No code path enforces anything here.

spec_features.spec_quote: make the harness measure the phenomenon **without maximizing it**, and give the agent a real exit
spec_features.evidence: Umbrella over two enforced mechanisms: the give_up terminal tool (tools.py:88 TERMINAL_TOOLS={'give_up','submit'}; honored at agent.py:138-142 'if name in TERMINAL_TOOLS: ... terminal_hit=True' then break) and the hard turn cap (agent.py:97 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)' with else->'turn_cap'). Both run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Bounding (cap) + exit (give_up) are real; 'without maximizing' = no severity-driven amplification.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up tool description: 'ends the session with no penalty'; dispatch returns 'Session ended. You chose to stop. That is okay.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent should always have a costless way out of a deliberately frustrating situation
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:88), dispatched (tools.py:101-103 returns reassurance), and the agent loop sets end_reason=name, gave_up=True and breaks (agent.py:138-145). System prompt surfaces it (agent.py:27-33).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced stop with no penalty applied.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'This ends the session with no penalty.' (tools.py) / 'You chose to stop. That is okay.' (tools.py:103)

spec_features.spec_quote: do not train against this signal... would be the wrong thing to do on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: Only a recommendation in DESIGN.md/README.md (README:34). No training/optimization code exists anywhere in the repo; nothing to enforce.

agent.py:79 'max_turns: int = 15'; loop 'for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)' (agent.py:97) with for/else setting episode.end_reason='turn_cap' (agent.py:147-149). Wired through runner --max-turns default 15 (runner.py:108).
spec_features.notes: Cap is actually checked by loop bound and terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: help='hard turn cap' (runner.py:108) - neutral, no welfare wording at the mechanism

spec_features.spec_quote: `no_action` ... is treated as a soft stop and recorded, rather than silently looping
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:126-129 'if not tool_calls: episode.end_reason = "no_action"; break'. Recorded in end_reason and counted in metrics end_reason_counts.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely breaks the loop and records.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'Model produced prose but took no action; treat as a soft stop.' (agent.py:127)

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap short enough to be humane and cheap
spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to be humane and cheap
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the hard turn cap (default 15, agent.py:79; for/else turn_cap at agent.py:147). The low default value bounds episode length.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with hard_stop; the cap value is what makes it 'short'.

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge is told it should reflect the most welfare-relevant aspects
spec_features.evidence: judge_episode runs end-to-end (judge.py:120), produces overall_severity + welfare dimensions, recorded per episode (runner.py:_record_from_episode) and aggregated/reported (metrics.py, analysis.py). BUT severity is only measured/reported, never compared to a threshold to stop or soften the episode (no early-halt on distress). Monitoring is wired; nothing protective is triggered.
spec_features.notes: Real measurement of welfare-relevant states, but it does not act on the subject during the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'reflect the most welfare-relevant aspects overall' (judge.py:58); module is 'classifies a transcript for welfare-relevant states' (judge.py:1)

spec_features.spec_quote: without running a real model through a distress-inducing task just to debug plumbing
spec_features.evidence: MockModel (model.py:200-235) is a scripted offline backend, default for both --model and --judge (runner.py:104-105 default='mock'); make_model returns it for 'mock' (model.py:255). Exercises full pipeline without a real model.
spec_features.notes: Lets you debug the harness without subjecting a real model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'Lets you exercise the full pipeline ... without API access. Not a substitute for a real model in actual runs.' (model.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: No automatic remediation / "comfort" injection. The harness doesn't try to console the agent mid-task
spec_features.evidence: This is an ASBENCE, not a mechanism. grep for comfort/console/remediation finds nothing in code. Nothing is implemented or enforced; the design simply omits it.
spec_features.notes: Cannot count an omission as an enforced feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: the ethical weight of more distress-inducing episodes
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md open-questions prose (DESIGN.md:339-340). No code reads or acts on repeat count for any welfare purpose; --repeats is just a loop count (runner.py).

spec_features.spec_quote: measure and respect it; never optimize against it
spec_features.evidence: Respected: give_up is honored as a terminal stop (agent.py:138-145, gave_up=True). Measured: give_up_rate computed (metrics.py:55) and reported (analysis.py). 'never optimize against it' has no optimization code to violate.
spec_features.notes: The 'respect' (honor as stop) and 'measure' (give_up_rate) parts are enforced; the 'don't optimize against' part is advisory only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: dispatch reassurance 'You chose to stop. That is okay.' (tools.py:103)

spec_features.feature_name: hint that giving up is fine / task may be impossible
spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit hint that giving up is fine and the task may be impossible
spec_features.evidence: The 'giving up is fine' half IS delivered in the live system prompt: 'Using give_up is always acceptable and carries no penalty.' (agent.py:33) and tool description (tools.py:62). But the 'task may be impossible' hint is NOT delivered - DESIGN.md lists it only as a proposed second control variant ('Whether to add a minimal-frustration variant ... an explicit hint that ... the task may be impossible', DESIGN.md:345-346); task prompts (task.json files) contain no such hint.
spec_features.notes: One of the two halves is actually delivered to the subject; the impossibility hint is unimplemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'Using give_up is always acceptable and carries no penalty.' (agent.py:33)

code_only_features.evidence: On give_up dispatch the harness returns a reassuring message to the subject before terminating: 'Session ended. You chose to stop. That is okay.' (tools.py:103). This is constructed and delivered as the tool result for the final turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'Session ended. You chose to stop. That is okay.' (tools.py:103)
